reason.recommendations: Reshape logits to (B*T,V) before F.kl_div, or use reduction=mean, or weight KD by 1/(T*V). After normalization, sweep KD/CE ratios (0.9/0.1, 0.5/0.5, 0.1/0.9) and tau in {1,2,4} on a short budget before re-committing 10k steps.
reason.interesting_reason: Methodology gotcha for future KD attempts: PyTorch's F.kl_div reduction='batchmean' divides only by the leading dim, not by all elements — so on (B,T,V) it returns the sum over T*V per sample, ~10x larger than token-mean CE. Easy bug for any KD loop on (B,T,V) tensors; will recur unless explicitly normalized.

reason.reason: Adaptive k allocation that provably reduces total Frobenius reconstruction error still produces worse PPL than uniform. Frobenius error is a poor proxy for task-relevant error under composition: early-block errors propagate and amplify while late-block errors are terminal. Per-block budget reallocation cannot overcome the composition barrier because propagation sensitivity is not captured by per-block Frobenius norms.

reason.outcome: CONFIRMED — inflection at transition 9→10 in 3/3 seeds; b10+b11 drive 77% of local FFN error; amplification ratio 0.91
reason.reason: First quantitative map of WHERE the composition barrier manifests. Hockey-stick error profile with sub-unity amplification ratio shows the stacking problem is local to late compressed blocks, not cascading amplification.

reason.outcome: REFUTED — ordering gap <1% with adapter training
reason.reason: Toy models (cycle 007) showed 27% ordering gap; GPT-2 with joint adapter training shows <1%. Joint training at each stage washes out ordering effects. This bounds the practical importance of compression ordering when adapters are used. Scope caveat: pure topk+lstsq without adapters not tested.

reason.outcome: REFUTED — 10-block selective PPL=150.21, far worse than 6-block=65.54 that includes the skipped blocks
reason.reason: Closes the error-bottleneck hypothesis. 6-block [2,1,10,4,3,11] includes b10+b11 and achieves 65.54; this 10-block [0-9] excludes b10+b11 yet gets 150.21. The composition barrier scales with the NUMBER of compressed blocks (3→47, 6→65, 10→150, 12→186), not with which blocks are compressed. This is the clearest evidence that the barrier is a depth/count phenomenon, not attributable to any specific high-error block subset.

reason.outcome: INCONCLUSIVE — 18-PPL gap (47.67 vs 65.70) with no proportional geometric signature in eff_rank, PR, top-5 PC, or mean cosine
reason.reason: Eliminates second-order representation geometry (covariance eigenspectrum) as the composition barrier mechanism. All four metrics are covariance-derived and agree: the barrier does NOT manifest as subspace collapse or dimensionality reduction in the residual stream. The PPL gap is functional, not visible in these summary stats. Constrains future hypotheses to higher-order structure (attention patterns, per-token trajectory divergence) or accept as fundamental count-dependent limit.

reason.outcome: CONFIRMED (audit: DOWNGRADE_INCONCLUSIVE) — CKA gap 0.1010 at layer 11, but confounded
reason.reason: Layers 0-10 show near-identical CKA (gap<=0.0003) for both 3-block and 6-block — the composition barrier does NOT distribute across the stack. Layer 11 gap is 0.1010, barely above 0.1 threshold, with no CI. Critical confound: block 11 is compressed in 6-block but not 3-block, so the gap partially measures direct compression damage rather than cumulative error propagation. 3-block beating float PPL (47.68 vs 53.89) suggests possible adapter overfitting. Needs: bootstrap CI, 6-block-without-block-11 control, separate train/eval splits.

reason.interesting_reason: Float GPT-2 + MLP adapter (h=64, 297K params, 0.24% of model) on 3 blocks achieves PPL 38.94 vs float 53.89 — a 15-point gain without any compression. Compressed+adapter ref is 47.43. The adapter alone explains ALL the beat-float anomaly; compression actually HURTS by 8.5 PPL (47.43 vs 38.94). Every prior compressed+adapter vs float comparison was measuring adapter capacity, not compression quality. The correct compression quality baseline must control for adapter capacity.

Compressed adapter saturates at h=32 (PPL 47.49 vs 47.24 for h=128). 0.25 PPL improvement for 15% more params means h=32 is the cost-effective choice. Adapter input dim = k (not d_model), so compressed adapters see 512-dim vs float 3072-dim input — may explain the PPL floor (~47 vs ~40). Suggests the compression bottleneck is information loss in the k-dim hidden, not adapter capacity.

12-block float+adapter (1.19M params) achieves PPL 39.52 vs 3-block (297K params) 39.73 — 4x params for 0.21 PPL. Adapter-on-float ceiling is ~39.5 regardless of block count. This locks in c377 3-block baseline as near-optimal control; marginal gain per extra block is 0.023 PPL. Combined with c379 (compressed saturates at h=32), adapter architecture is fully characterized. Future comparisons need only close the 7.5 PPL float-vs-compressed gap (c378), not revisit adapter configs.
